title: Orthogonal component inner product sum
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by $\iota$, is orthonormal for the inner product given by expectation under $\pi$, and one designated basis vector is the constant-one function. For any natural number $n$ and any real-valued functions $f,g$ on $\Omega^n$, their inner product under the product probability measure is the sum, over all subsets $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, of the inner products of their Fourier components supported on $S$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
A basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ indexed by $\iota$
The designated basis vector is constant one
